html:
The first major battle of the First Crusade, fought from 14 May to 19 June 1097 at Nicaea in northwest Anatolia, then the capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum.

The sultan, Kilij Arslan I, was away fighting other Turks when the crusaders arrived, and the army he brought back was beaten outside the walls. But the city lay on a lake and could still be supplied by water. Emperor Alexios I had boats dragged overland and launched on the lake, closing the ring.

The garrison then made a secret deal with Alexios's envoy and surrendered to the Byzantines, not the crusaders. The crusaders woke to see the emperor's flags on the towers and were barred from looting. Alexios paid them off with gifts, but the episode sowed lasting distrust between the crusaders and Byzantium. The crusade marched on, won at Dorylaeum about two weeks later, and two years later ended with the capture of Jerusalem. The sultans moved their capital to Konya.
sum: The first major battle of the First Crusade, fought from 14 May to 19 June 1097 at Nicaea in northwest Anatolia, then the capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum.
